And no one of them escaped except Muḥyī the geometer and astronomer.
For this very man related to me:
"On that day, while al-Malik al-Nāṣir was sitting in his tent,
and had summoned me to him and was asking me about his horoscope,
then a certain great Mongol chief came at the noon hour,
and with him about fifty Mongols.
And al-Malik al-Nāṣir went out to meet him.
And he said to him,
'There is a banquet today with the King of Kings,
and he tells you to take your brother, your sons, and the nobles who are with you,
and come there.'
And al-Malik al-Nāṣir arose and took with him his own people and his nobles, about twenty persons,
and they mounted and went.
And shortly afterwards, twenty horsemen came to us at the tents and said,
'Let the horsemen and the pages {or: youths} come,
and let none remain except the servants who strike the tents, the cooks, and the shepherds.'
And when we had mounted,
they led us through deep ravines,
and brought us down to where the Mongol nobles were encamped,
with others standing before them.
And when we approached and they began to speak with us,
suddenly the Mongols leaped from behind us,
and each one seized one of us.
And I signaled to the nobles,
'I am an astronomer,
and I know the movements of the heavens.'
And they called me and made me sit behind them.
And the rest they led a little further off and slaughtered them.
And likewise they had killed al-Malik al-Nāṣir, his brother, and the nobles.
But his sons they did not kill;
and behold, down to this day they are prisoners with them.
Afterwards they went and brought also those little ones who had remained in the tents,
and them too they killed."
